strengths: Clear and well-motivated core idea: relaxing MTP's exact prediction to ranking is intuitive and computationally efficient, requiring only one additional linear layer versus MTP's multiple transformer layers
Systematic experimental design: models trained at three scales with matched parameter counts across NTP/MTP/TOP for fair comparison
Consistent improvements on standard NLP benchmarks: TOP outperforms both NTP and MTP on most tasks, with larger gains at 7B scale (e.g., +3.0 SciQ, +6.63 TriviaQA)
Strong presentation: clear figures (Figure 1 effectively illustrates TOP), explicit algorithms, detailed hyperparameters in Table 1, and accessible writing
Computational efficiency: no additional parameters needed when adjusting window size, unlike MTP which requires new transformer layers per additional future token
Reproducibility support: code promised, optimized Triton kernel implementation detailed, comprehensive hyperparameter specification
weaknesses: Weak empirical support for core motivation: Figure 2 relies on a single 16M parameter model, which is too small to generalize. No systematic analysis of why MTP loss curves behave this way across scales, nor evidence this difficulty persists in larger models where MTP actually works

Critical unexplained phenomenon: TOP exhibits higher NTP training loss than NTP baseline yet achieves better downstream performance (all scales for Lambada). The regularization hypothesis is purely speculative and unsubstantiated. This contradicts the stated mechanism and requires rigorous investigation

Modest and inconsistent improvements with no significance testing: many gains <1% (PIQA: +0.92, +0.65, -0.60), several 7B tasks degrade (Social IQa -0.46), missing error bars and multiple-seed evaluation despite appearing to be single runs

Incomplete critical evaluation: missing generative tasks (coding, summarization) where auxiliary objectives provide strongest benefits—these are deferred to future work despite being central to motivating auxiliary losses. Only 52-104B tokens training budget (very small by 2026 standards)

Unjustified design choice: window size set to sequence length (4096), meaning TOP predicts order over entire remaining sequence rather than nearby tokens as motivation suggests. No ablation on window size or justification for this decision

Potentially unfair MTP baseline: reducing MTP trunk by 3 layers to match parameters may not be optimal; original paper's configurations not explored. DeepSeek V3 uses N=2 (not N=4) but only acknowledged as future work. Different architectural modifications may yield different conclusions

Missing methodological rigor: no ablations on loss weight (1:1), window size, or alternative ranking losses; no sensitivity analysis; single training runs without confidence intervals; limited computational overhead analysis despite claiming efficiency

Limited scope and scalability questions: models only reach 7B (modest by current standards); unclear if benefits persist at larger scales (13B+) or with larger training budgets (>100B tokens). No guidance on how to set window size for different scenarios

strengths: Clear motivation with empirical evidence (Figure 2) that MTP becomes increasingly difficult for farther tokens, supporting the case for a simpler ranking-based approach
Significant computational efficiency gains: TOP requires only one unembedding layer (2DV FLOPs) versus MTP/DS-MTP's multiple transformer blocks ((N-1)(24D²) FLOPs)
Consistent improvements across 9 standard NLP benchmarks, math/code tasks, and synthetic star graph problem across three model sizes (340M, 1.8B, 7B)
Better scaling properties than MTP—unlike MTP which underperforms at 7B, TOP continues to improve relative to NTP, suggesting better scalability
Comprehensive experimental setup with matched parameter counts, training curves, ablation studies on window size and loss weighting, and clear algorithmic description
Well-written paper with effective visualizations and thorough reproducibility details in appendices
weaknesses: Modest improvements over NTP: mostly 1-3% on standard benchmarks with no statistical significance testing, confidence intervals, or multi-run variance analysis

Critical concern about DS-MTP implementation: performs dramatically worse than MTP, contradicting DeepSeek-V3's success. Authors acknowledge 'unusually low performance' but investigation is incomplete, raising questions about implementation reliability across all comparisons
Self-speculative decoding results show TOP is substantially worse than MTP/DS-MTP (~1.5 vs ~2.5 acceptance at 7B), negating a key practical advantage and limiting deployment utility

Insufficient analysis of mechanisms: no investigation into what representations TOP learns differently than NTP, no error analysis by task/benchmark, and limited theoretical justification for why ranking by proximity should improve language modeling
Scale limitations: largest model is 7B with 104B token training; unclear if approach scales to modern pretraining standards (70B+); authors acknowledge but don't resolve compute constraints

Incomplete ablations and unexplained design choices: exploration stops at α=0.9 for loss weighting (higher values unexplored), ListNet loss choice not justified against alternatives, effectiveness of TOP-only training not empirically validated
Reproducibility gaps: code link appears blank in manuscript; no random seed information, multiple run statistics, or verification of baseline implementations against original papers
Inconsistent results on some benchmarks and unclear connection between synthetic star graph task and real language understanding gains

strengths: Clear motivation with empirical evidence (Figure 2) that MTP training is increasingly difficult for distant tokens
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple model sizes (340M, 1.8B, 7B) and diverse domains (NLP benchmarks, math, code, synthetic tasks)
Significant computational efficiency gains over MTP: O(2DV) vs O((N-1)24D²) FLOPs, with only a single linear layer overhead
Synthetic star graph pathfinding task provides compelling validation that TOP can learn look-ahead when NTP fails
Honest limitations discussion acknowledging compute constraints
weaknesses: Improvements are modest and inconsistent (typically 0.2-1.5%) without statistical significance testing or error bars; unclear if gains exceed noise margins
TOP significantly underperforms on self-speculative decoding (1.54 tokens/pass vs MTP's 2.49), contradicting MTP's primary practical advantage and undermining practical motivation
Severe experimental anomalies with DS-MTP on code/math tasks (e.g., 2.65% vs 39.20% on GSM8K) suggest implementation or hyperparameter issues that cast doubt on entire experimental setup
Weak theoretical justification for why token ordering is the correct relaxation of MTP; ListNet loss borrowed from IR without deep connection to language modeling objectives
High hyperparameter sensitivity: window size ablation (Table 7) shows large variance across benchmarks; optimal loss weighting α=0.9 contradicts 'auxiliary objective' framing
Limited scale evaluation (only up to 7B parameters) insufficient for 2026; unclear if benefits generalize to modern 13B+ models
Architectural confounds: MTP/DS-MTP use reduced depth to match parameters, making it unclear whether improvements stem from the TOP objective or architectural differences
Missing interpretability analysis of what representations TOP learns differently; no probing studies or representation analysis to understand the mechanism

strengths: Well-motivated simplification of MTP: the observation that exact future token prediction becomes increasingly difficult (Figure 2) naturally motivates a ranking-based alternative using learning-to-rank loss
Significant architectural efficiency: TOP requires only 2DV FLOPs vs. (N-1)(24D²) for MTP with comparable or better performance, making it more scalable

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: consistent evaluation across three model scales, nine standard NLP benchmarks, generative tasks (math/code), and a synthetic pathfinding task demonstrating clear patterns

Consistent improvements on standard NLP benchmarks: TOP outperforms NTP, MTP, and DS-MTP baselines across most tasks and scales, with particularly strong synthetic task results (100% accuracy on star graph pathfinding)
Strong reproducibility: detailed hyperparameters in appendices, clear algorithm specification, optimized Triton kernel implementation, honest limitations discussion, and promised code release
Useful ablation studies: investigation of window size effects and loss weighting ratios provides insight into method behavior and design choices
weaknesses: Limited practical deployment value: inference cost is identical to NTP (TOP head removed at inference), and TOP significantly underperforms MTP/DS-MTP on self-speculative decoding (1.52 vs. 2.39-3.03 accepted tokens/pass for 7B), forfeiting MTP's concrete speed advantage

Modest magnitude of improvements: many benchmark gains are 1-3% absolute; no statistical significance testing or error bars provided; improvements on code tasks are explicitly described as 'more mixed' without clear TOP advantage

Problematic baseline comparison: DS-MTP shows unusually poor performance especially on math/code tasks; author explanation of overfitting is speculative; raises concerns about implementation correctness or fair comparison setup

Hyperparameter sensitivity inadequately addressed: Table 7 shows substantial variance across tasks and window sizes (e.g., LAMBADA perplexity degrades at W>16; SciQ varies 75.70→80.00); limited guidance on selecting window size in practice for new domains

Loss weighting finding contradicts auxiliary objective framing: α=0.9 (TOP-dominant loss) outperforms default α=0.5; suggests TOP may be replacing rather than complementing NTP; claim of 'stronger learning signal' lacks deeper investigation

Limited scale validation: maximum 7B model size; authors acknowledge inability to test on larger models due to compute constraints; unclear if improvements persist or scale to 13B, 70B+ models typical in 2026

Weak motivation for why ranking helps: Figure 2 shows lower TOP loss but doesn't establish causality to better learning; theoretical connection to teacher-forcing critique could be tighter; largely empirical without principled justification

Incomplete failure mode analysis: no clear characterization of task categories where MTP outperforms TOP; sparse discussion of when TOP underperforms (e.g., some code generation tasks); star graph results show only success cases
